# Portenv

> Portenv — your product, built by a team of AI agents (Portenv is short for portable environment; also heard as 'port env'). Each agent gets a role, its own user account and its own copy of your code, inside a workspace sealed off from your Mac. They build, review and hand work to each other. Anything that matters waits for your yes.

Each project gets an encrypted workspace ("box") that moves between your Mac and your own servers. You pick a ready-made team of agents with one command (Starter, App product team or Orchestrate; choosing it in the app comes next); each agent has its own role, its own user and only the access its job needs, and decisions wait for your answer in Needs you.

Status: in development. The Mac app is not available to download yet.

## What it is

- A native Mac app (macOS 26 or later, Apple silicon) and a command-line tool, `portenv`.
- Each box is encrypted on your device before it is saved, and saves as you go.
- Open source: the whole public repository, the Mac app included, is Apache-2.0: the app, the runner, the in-box agent and the save format.
- Works with your own servers and storage, without a Portenv account.

## Agents

You invite an agent to one box, see what it does, and can revoke it at any time. Agents never get your encryption keys.

Ways in, in the order they are being built:

1. SSH and the `portenv` command-line tool, with a published skill, for a box on your own server.
2. Webhooks: your agent is told when a box needs it, for example when a tool is waiting for an answer.
3. MCP on the agent's computer (stdio).
4. Remote MCP on your own server.
5. A web terminal on your own server, for agents that only have a browser.

## Short links

- https://portenv.com/cli: install the command-line tool (coming soon)
- https://portenv.com/skill: the skill for agents (coming soon)
- https://portenv.com/mcp: connect over MCP (coming soon)
